mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.0% per annum signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in labor force participation (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic expansion, which reduces recession risk and increases corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both PAYEMS and INDPRO increase (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 2.0% and sustained for 3 months), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during the 3-month period when FEDFUNDS rises above 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) indicates a tight labor market, which typically correlates with strong consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) above 1500.0 thousand units signals strong consumer demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and corporate revenue growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1500.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and residential sales (RSAFS) reflects broad-based economic expansion, which increases corporate profitability and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both INDPRO and RSAFS increase (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.0% per annum indicates sustained inflation, which typically leads to a 60-day period of monetary tightening and reduced equity market returns due to higher discount rates and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
